Town of Bow Recycling and Solid Waste Committee September 1, 2026 Meeting Draft Meeting Minutes To:​ David Stack, Town Manager cc:​ Bow Administrative Assistant, Committee Webpage, Recycling Committee Members Re: ​ Recycling and Solid Waste Committee Minutes for September 1, 2026 Meeting (DRAFT) Date:​ September 1, 2026 Committee Member Attendees: Sherri Cheney, Deb Unger, Beth Titus, and Irene Hou. Other Attendees: Greg Rule, Dunbarton Transfer Station Manager, Helga Bouchard, Dunbarton Resident MEETING BEGAN AT 7:05 P.M. 1.​ Review of June Meeting Minutes To be approved at the October meeting. 2.​ Recycling Tipping Fees –Rates Sherri Cheney reported on tipping fees for recyclables.

The tipping fees per ton were $129.97 for June and $143.77 for July. Sherri noted that tipping fees have increased and questioned whether we should consider other options. It was decided that we would continue to monitor fees for now. 3. ​ Recycling and Solid Waste Totals Sherri reported on collection amounts for recycling and solid waste. Single stream recycling was 77.56 tons for June and 72.56 tons for July. Trash was 201.21 tons for June and 206.20 tons for July. 4. Renewal Garden and Compost Update The compost program continues to run smoothly and be well used. 5. Status of Terracycle Containers Since the last meeting, Irene sent in a full bag of snack pouches for recycling.

Irene updated the committee on our request to redeem points. Terracycle redeems points twice yearly, so our points will be paid out in January 2027. Our request was for 46,337 points = $463.37. 6. HOUSEHOLD HAZARDOUS WASTE DAY October 17, 2026 Sherri led a discussion on managing HHWD on October 17, 2026. In regard to management of local items, it was discussed that previously Woody Bowne (prior Supervisor of the Dunbarton Transfer Station) had rented a U-Haul and coordinated disposal of these items. Bow paid $350 to Dunbarton for coordinating the disposal in addition to the percentage of fees for Bow items.

Greg Rule, current Dunbarton Transfer Station Manager, stated he will manage the transportation and disposal of these local items to North Coast Services. Greg will also bring cardboard boxes for collecting tube fluorescent bulbs. Bow will pay Dunbarton $350 for this service as well the percentage of the cost of Bow’s recyclables. For waste oil, Sherri reported that last year, we had collected about 1.5-275 gallon tanks which were transported to Mr. Paul Locke and accepted by him free of charge. Greg Rule stated that he has 2 local sources (Weare and a Dunbarton resident) that accept 50 gallon barrels without a fee.

It was decided that Greg will contact the town of Dunbarton and his contacts and Sherri will contact Paul Locke. Greg and Sherri will then decide on the best available option for coordinating tanks, transport and disposal of waste oil. For electronics, Sherri will contact our vendor, American Retroworks Inc. 2 weeks prior to HHWD to confirm. The updated price list is posted on the town website. As an alternative to HHWD, Deb mentioned that Best Buy will accept computers for recycling and they treat the computer to ensure private information is removed. There was a discussion regarding volunteers to assist on HHWD. Members will encourage friends/family to participate.

Sherri reported that she updated the contract with our vendor for HHWD, NH Recycles, and forwarded it to town manager, David Stack. Once he signs it, she will forward it to NH Recycles. Assignment of jobs: ●​ Deb will post on our Facebook page and submit an article to the Bow Times. Deb will drop off flyers around town including the municipal building, Bow Rec Building and library. Flyers include education on HHWD, disposal of paint, and the impact of recyclables on the environment. ●​ Beth will submit HHWD information to the Concord Monitor Town Crier and arrange posting of the banner about 1 month prior to HHWD. ●​ Greg will bring 1-2 wagons to HHWD to assist with transport of items.

●​ Sherri will ask Taj to arrange for a lined dumpster from Casella for trash from HHWD as well as a container to recycle cardboard boxes. ●​ Sherri will ask Heath to arrange use of the town’s electronic sign for 2 weeks prior to HHWD and for schools to advertise on the school sign and in the school newsletter. ●​ Sherri will place 10 lawn signs around town (after the current primary signs are gone) and coordinate signs to assist with traffic on HHWD. 7. Trex Program: Plastic bag and Film Collection The program and collection have been working well.

Given the hassle and recent changes to the rewards program, we are not currently weighing and uploading pictures of weights for now since we have already received our allotted annual gift. We will plan to restart again in April 2027 when we can begin working towards our next annual $100 gift. 8.​ HELPSY Helpsy collected 430 pounds in April-June and 559 pounds so far in the July-September period. 9. Other business Bow’s volunteer appreciation BBQ is September 10th at the Old Town Hall. All committee members are encouraged to attend.

Sherri reported she will attend the Joint Meeting with the Board of Selectmen and Town Committee which will now be held on Tuesday, October 13th at 5:00 pm in Meeting Room A. Sherri will attend and other members are invited to attend as well. Next Committee meeting is October 6, 2026. Meeting adjourned 8:39 p.m. Respectfully Submitted, Irene Hou

CIP Committee –Approved Minutes Page | 1 August 31, 2026 Town of Bow Capital Improvement Committee August 31, 2026 Approved Minutes The Capital Improvement Program (CIP) Committee met, Monday, August 31, 2026 at 5:30 PM in Room C at the Municipal Building, 10 Grandview Road, Bow, NH. Committee members present: Vice Chair Glenn Dugas (Citizen Representative), Harry Judd (Citizen Representative), Jenna Reardon (Alt. School Board Representative), Angela Brennan (Selectboard Representative), Jonathan Pietrangelo (Planning Board Representative), and Jeffrey Knight (Budget Committee Representative). Absent (excused):

Mark Davis (Citizen Representative) and Martin Osterloh (School Board Representative). Also present: Finance Director Cheryl Lindner, Facilities Manager Chris Andrews, SAU Business Administrator Duane Ford, Library Director Kaitlin Camidge and Library Trustee Shari Vincent-Crisp. I. Call to Order The Vice Chair called the meeting to order at 5:30 PM. II. Approval of Minutes – Harry Judd moved to approve the minutes of July 28, 2026. Jeff Knight seconded the motion. Vice Chair Dugas called for comments. Harry Judd wanted to clarify Section III Department Reviews – Parks and Recreation to note Director Little stated the contribution of $150,000 couldn’t be maintained ad infinitum.

Both the motion maker and seconder agreed to the revisions. A vote was called on the revised minutes which were carried by unanimous vote of the Committee. III. Department Reviews Bow School District – Business Administrator Ford gave a brief synopsis of several school projects completed over the summer. i.e. all projects in the infield and replacing the flat section of the roof of the high school. The Bow Elementary School (BES) renovation/addition is complete. The district was approved, at the annual school meeting, to draw $500,000 CIP funds. They have only drawn $46,000. CIP projects projected to be completed in 2027-28 include: a Blue Light Warning System for each of the three schools.

This was a recommendation from a safety audit performed on the buildings. Cost is estimated at $40,000 each. Bow Memorial School (BMS) - abate and replace the remaining asbestos flooring, estimated cost $62,974, extend irrigation to the remaining sports fields, $75,000. There has been some discussion about the track at BMS and whether to repair or remove it because the high school also has a regulation track. The Committee would like to see the track fixed if the decision is to keep it. Administrator Ford will check on the status. Bow High School (BHS) - LED lighting, $50,000; replacing the roof on the gym portion of the building (Phase 2), $252,000.

Complete replacement of the HVAC units on the BHS building is being proposed over a 3- to 4-year period, total estimated cost of $2,850,000, to avoid having to bond for the project. Baker Free Library – Library Director Kaitlin Camidge explained changes/adjustments have been made to some of the projects listed on the library’s CIP. After much discussion, Committee members decided they would like to have the library director come back to the Committee with an explanation and revised information for further discussion. They suggested adding items to the listing which will eventually have to be replaced to allow for better tracking of the projects.

There were questions about what was included, or not, in bids/quotes for the projects. There was also some discussion on whether to put the HVAC replacement in a separate warrant article or leave it in CIP. CIP Committee –Approved Minutes Page | 2 August 31, 2026 Buildings and Facilities Department – Facilities Manager Chris Andrews reviewed the department’s proposed CIP projects. Some of the information and decisions on the proposed projects may change depending on input of the Buildings and Facilities Advisory Committee (BFAC) after they meet.

There was much discussion about the municipal building parking lot paving and safety concerns and replacement of the 2013 truck and plow, currently being used for plowing of municipal lots. The Committee mentioned adding “place-holder price(s)” until final pricing is available. Further explanation is needed for some items pending decisions made by the BFAC. V. Meeting Dates - The Committee decided to hold the next CIP meeting on September 14, 2026, 5:30PM in Room B at the Municipal Building. VI. Adjourn Upon a motion by Harry Judd and a second by Jenna Reardon, it was unanimously voted to adjourn the meeting at 8:15 PM. Respectfully submitted Wendy Gilman, Recording Secretary

TOWN OF BOW Conservation Commission 10 Grandview Road, Bow, New Hampshire 03304 Phone (603) 223-3970 Fax (603) 225-2982 Website: www.bownh.gov Email: conservation@bownh.gov Conservation Commission Approved Minutes Monday, August 17, 2026 The regular meeting of the Bow Conservation Commission was held on Monday, August 17, 2026, at 7:00 PM in Room C of the Municipal Office Building, 10 Grandview Road. Chair Crystall called the meeting to order at 7:00 PM. Commissioners present: Sandy Crystall, Lisa Lindquist, Mary Farrell, Tom O'Donovan and Dik Dagavarian Other attendees: Ginger Iverson, Recording Secretary 1.

UMWA Invoice Chair Crystall reviewed the annual membership and support invoice from the Upper Merrimack Watershed Association (UMWA). She noted the organization’s continued work in watershed protection, water quality monitoring, habitat conservation, regional planning initiatives, and technical assistance to communities throughout the Merrimack River watershed. The Commission agreed that the Association continues to be a valuable regional partner. Mr. O’Donovan made a motion, seconded by Mr. Dagavarian, to approve payment of $150 for the UMWA Municipal Support invoice. Vote: 5:0. 2. Land Conservation Work – Status – Non-Public Session RSA 91-A:3,II(d) Mr.

O’Donovan made a motion, seconded by Ms. Farrell, to enter non-public session per RSA 91- A:3, II (d) Consideration of the acquisition, sale or lease of real or personal property which, if discussed in public, would likely benefit a party or parties whose interests are adverse to those of the general community. 5:0 Roll Call Vote: Lisa Lindquist – Yes; Tom O’Donovan – Yes; Dik Dagavarian – Yes; Mary Farrell – Yes; Sandy Crystall – Yes Recording was turned off at 7:02 p.m. and entered into non-public session. Public Session was reconvened at 7:26 p.m. Ms. Linquist made a motion to seal the non-public minutes per RSA 91-A:3, II. Motion was seconded by Ms. Farrell. 5:0 Roll Call Vote:

Lisa Lindquist – Yes; Tom O’Donovan – Yes; Dik Dagavarian – Yes; Mary Farrell – Yes; Sandy Crystall – Yes Conservation Commission Approved Minutes 08/17/2026 2 3. Robertson Trail Plan for Construction Mr. O’Donovan reported that preparations for the Robertson Trail bridge project were progressing. Lumber had been ordered and delivery was anticipated during the following week. Construction hardware was already on hand and volunteers had been recruited to assist on Monday, August 24, 2026 with unloading materials. Commission members discussed the anticipated construction schedule, including material delivery, and volunteer coordination.

Chair Crystall requested that the volunteers review the plans. Construction will begin on Friday, August 28, 2026. Chair Crystall noted that signatures are needed on the wetlands permit to be posted prior to construction activity and that permit posting should be placed where visible. Permit completion documentation must be submitted following construction. The Commission members then discussed the condition of two deteriorated culverts located along the trail corridor. The Town of Bow’s Department of Public Works offered to replace the pipe with cast iron at no cost; however, the approved trail notification requires replacement in kind. Ms. Lindquist made a motion, seconded by Mr.

Dagavarian, to approve the $3,500 proposal based upon a recent quote and in accordance with the existing permit, to replace the two deteriorated culverts along the Robertson Trail corridor. The motion passed by a vote of 4:1, with Mr. O’Donovan opposed. The possibility of a future ribbon-cutting event for the trail improvements was also discussed. 4. Conservation Land Management Chair Crystall provided updates regarding several ongoing stewardship projects, easement matters, and survey-related issues. Mr. O’Donovan received an update concerning a survey review involving a property boundary question at Merrill Crossing.

Town Forester Ron Klemarczyk completed his final report and provided findings to Mr. O’Donovan, Mr. Eric Thum, Stewardship Director for Bow Open Spaces, and to the surveying company. The survey company has reportedly requested further review by the retired surveyor responsible for that work. Chair Crystall also reported follow-up efforts concerning survey proposals associated with the Dufour property donation. Discussion continued regarding stewardship concerns associated with the Fish and Game easement on the town conservation land by Briarwood Drive. Chair Crystall discussed easement language, and questions concerning allowed activities within protected areas.

Chair Crystall will work with Code Enforcement Officer Will Dinsmore to address the issues surrounding this easement. Questions about clearing on Westover Lane conservation property were discussed. Chair Crystall noted the need to verify property boundaries and evaluate possible encroachments affecting open space and conservation lands. Community Development Director Karri Makinen will ask Code Enforcement Officer Will Dinsmore to look into this matter. Conservation Commission Approved Minutes 08/17/2026 3 5. VLAP (Volunteer Lake Assessment Program) Chair Crystall noted that the VLAP sampling results for July had been received.

The sampling location at the inlet to Town Pond that is downgradient of Bow Memorial School and parking lot, continues to have high levels of chloride despite being well after its seasonal use in the winter. Additional information gathering and outreach may occur in the future. On a groundwater quality concern, Mr. O’Donovan summarized recent correspondence between local officials and the New Hampshire Department of Transportation concerning road salt application practices along Route 3-A. Mr.

O’Donovan discussed evidence suggesting that chloride concentrations in the Route 3-A area may no longer be exhibiting normal seasonal fluctuations and could be reaching long-term accumulation levels within groundwater systems. Mr. O'Donovan mentioned recent responses from state transportation officials and discussed possible opportunities for reduced-salt roadway management practices. Drinking Water Protection Committee members noted that some progress appears to have been made in establishing a dialogue concerning alternative winter maintenance approaches. 6.

Other Items • Planning Board projects under review – During a site walk at the Mariner Tower property, the Commission observed what appeared to be evidence of an ephemeral stream channel flowing from the wetland. The applicant subsequently modified the plan to identify the ephemeral stream, which was consistent with the wetland scientist’s report noting seasonal water outflow from the wetland. Chair Crystall contacted NHDES to confirm whether the ephemeral stream is a jurisdictional resource and they confirmed that it is jurisdictional, although it is not subject to the stream crossing rules. Ms.

Makinen, Community Development Director, subsequently spoke with the applicant regarding how they intended to address the resource. The Commission planned to see what revisions or additional information the applicant would provide at the upcoming Planning Board meeting. The Commission discussed correspondence from residents regarding wildlife observations documented near the project area. The Commission noted that there were other issues as well and did not expect a decision on the project at that meeting.

• NHDES wetland rule changes & NHACC related – topics/meetings – Fish & Game Commission – Chair Crystall provided an update regarding the July 2026 New Hampshire Association of Conservation Commissions’ activities and ongoing Department of Environmental Services rulemaking efforts. Discussions highlighted prime wetlands including proposed revisions affecting prime wetlands regulations, efforts to clarify administrative procedures, and opportunities for local commissions to comment on future regulatory changes. Chair Crystall will post the draft proposed rules, as they are public information.

Proposed language in the draft describes that for corrections or new prime wetland designations, if a landowner requests that a prime wetland boundary be delineated in the field, the delineation is required to be completed. Chair Crystall expressed concern that this requirement could become costly for a town. Apparently this requirement is based on language in the law. The Commission also discussed members of the Fish and Game Commission seeking to improve communication and engagement with local conservation commissions around the state.

Chair Crystall suggested considering a roundtable discussion Conservation Commission Approved Minutes 08/17/2026 4 with other towns and inviting the Fish and Game Commissioner to attend. • Conditions for approved projects – In response to questions raised by Commissioners at the previous Commission meeting, Chair Crystall provided the Planning Board conditions for wetland CUP approval for the Belanger property, that included the removal of the shed from the buffer. Also shared were the Planning Board conditions for approval of the Kearsarge Bow LF LLC (Solar Farm), which requires the project developer to return to the Commission.

Chair Crystall clarified that removal of the Belanger shed is a condition of approval and therefore must be completed. Mr. O'Donovan asked who would verify that the shed had actually been removed, and Will Dinsmore, Code Enforcement Officer, was identified as the person who would likely conduct the site verification. The Commission agreed that this should remain an open item and that, sometime in the fall, they should follow up with Mr. Dinsmore to confirm that he had inspected the site and verified the shed’s removal. Regarding the solar farm, the preliminary approval conditions confirm that the applicant would need to return to the Commission as part of the approval process.

• BeaverCON – Chair Crystall requested consideration of financial assistance to attend BeaverCON, a national conference being held in Minnesota, focused on beaver ecology, wetland restoration, ecosystem management, and nature-based resilience strategies. The Commission members discussed the educational value of the conference and the benefits of bringing current restoration information back to the Commission. Mr. O’Donovan made a motion, seconded by Ms. Linquist, to approve reimbursement of up to $600 for conference registration costs for Chair Crystall, on condition that Chair Crystall speak with conference representatives about bringing BeaverCON to New Hampshire in the future. Vote:

4:0:1 with Chair Crystall abstaining. • Zoning review – Chair Crystall asked the Commissioners to consider items for further review. She will also review whether the descriptions of the Commission’s jurisdiction and its ordinance are all inclusive. • Conservation Project Review – Chair Crystall suggested conducting quarterly project reviews, rather than monthly. Mr. O’Donovan noted that projects that are not regularly reviewed may not get completed. Chair Crystall encouraged Conservation Commission members to volunteer their assistance with projects.

• Ideas for Bow’s 300th Anniversary – The Commission discussed possible participation in activities associated with Bow's upcoming 300th Anniversary celebration. Mr. O’Donovan proposed establishment of three engraved stone benches representing Bow's first, second, and third centuries. The benches would be placed within conservation lands or other significant public locations and could include inscriptions commemorating the town's history and commitment to conservation. The Commissioners expressed strong support for the concept and discussed possible locations, designs, installation logistics, and funding considerations. Mr.

O’Donovan agreed to begin gathering information regarding costs and potential vendors. Chair Crystall suggested identifying events for active participation for the 300th, as well. • Town Pond – The Fire Department’s hose discharge activities appear to have caused a rut- like channel leading into the pond and flattened vegetation. Chair Crystall communicated with the Fire Chief, who indicated that the damage may have resulted from fire training exercises. Chair Crystall would like to recommend that when plans for the site are created, Conservation Commission Approved Minutes 08/17/2026 5 the Town consider installing a semi-hard surface in the area to be used for hose discharge. Mr.

O’Donovan suggested that education on appropriate practices may be needed. • Land Use Change Tax – Chair Crystall reported the available funds for future conservation projects and acquisitions. Future events/workshops/trainings: • Select Board review with the Committee Chairs 9/22/2026 – Chair Crystall noted that the Commission shares updates on its activities and asked the Commissioners to consider items for which the Commission may seek assistance. Mr. O’Donovan discussed the topic of herbicide spraying by Eversource and the need to monitor it. • NHACC annual meeting & conference 11/7/2026 Unapproved Minutes: July 13, 2026 Ms.

Farrell made a motion to approve the July 13, 2026 minutes as amended. The motion was seconded by Ms. Lindquist Vote 4:0:1 with Mr. Dagavarian abstaining. Adjournment Mr. Dagavarian made a motion to adjourn the meeting. The motion was seconded by Ms. Lindquist. Vote 5:0. The meeting adjourned at 8:20 p.m. Next meeting: September 14, 2026 Respectfully submitted, Ginger Iverson Recording Secretary

1 August 11, 2026 Board of Selectmen Meeting Approved Minutes August 11, 2026 On Tuesday, July 14, 2026, at 5:30 p.m., the Board of Selectmen met in Meeting Room A, at the Bow Municipal Building, 10 Grandview Road, Bow, NH 03304. This meeting was also live streamed on YouTube https://www.youtube.com/live/OD-cmW_izAw?si=hAB3a7gIK_0-9phW I. CALL TO ORDER Chair McDaniel called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. Present: Chair Kip McDaniel, Selectman Chris Nicolopoulos, Selectwoman Eleana Colby, Town Manager David Stack, Finance Director Cheryl Lindner, Executive Assistant Tonia Lindquist and members of the public. Not present: Selectwoman Brennan and Vice Chair Flanagan II.

PUBLIC COMMENT - None III. PUBLIC HEARINGS 1. Grant from NH Department of Environmental Services to extend water main from the City of Concord Municipal Water Systems pursuant to RSA 31:95-b The Board held a public hearing to discuss the acceptance of a grant from the New Hampshire Department of Environmental Services to extend a water main from the City of Concord Municipal Water Systems to Bow Junction to address PFAS, Chlorides, lead and copper corrosion, arsenic, radon, hardness and MtBE present within the system. Chair McDaniel opened the public hearing at 6:03 p.m. There being no comments, the public hearing was closed.

A MOTION was made by Selectman Nicolopoulos and seconded by Selectwoman Colby to accept the grant from the State of New Hampshire in the amount of $1,500,000 under the Disadvantaged Community Grant Program Funds and to authorize Town Manager David Stack to sign any documents necessary for the Town of Bow. MOTION PASSED 3-0. IV. MEETINGS 1. Community Building Discussion – Citizen Group Residents Jeff Knight, Harry Judd, Glenn Dugas, and Colleen Hunter appeared before the Board to provide an update on their efforts to develop an affordable Community Building for the Town.

The group is requestingg authorization to issue a Request for Proposals (RFP) to obtain a firm design- build cost estimate that can be presented to taxpayers in March 2027. The proposed facility would be 2 August 11, 2026 approximately 17,000 square feet and include a full-size gymnasium. The location of the building has not yet been determined. The group is recommending $7,500 to retain an independent third-party professional to act on behalf of the Town. This consultant would review the RFP for completeness and evaluate the proposals received to ensure the pricing is reasonable and consistent with current market conditions.

Selectman Nicolopoulos feels the Board owes it to the community to start coming up with a plan considering this community has made the commitment to put funds away to support the project. His recommendation for location would be the School Forest. A MOTION was made by Selectwoman Colby and seconded by Selectman Nicolopoulos to expend up to $7,500 from the Recreation Revolving Fund to cover the cost of the review of an RFP for completeness and review of the quotes when they come in for the community building. MOTION PASSED 3-0. Mr. Knight invited a Select Board member to join the resident group, or the group can report back to the Board, Chair McDaniel volunteered to join the group. 2.

Quarterly Financial Report and End of Yar Report – Finance Director Cheryl Lindner Director Cheryl Lindner presented the 4th Quarter Financial Report and End of Year Report. (attached) While Director Lindner had the floor, the Board elected to move Agenda Item No. 4, Water Capital Replacement/System Improvement Fund Withdrawal Request, to this point in the meeting so that Director Lindner could address the matter. The Board reviewed Director Lindner’s memo and the accompanying invoices related to repairs resulting from a major water leak that occurred in June.

Director Lindner requested authorization to withdraw $21,002.63 from the Water Capital Replacement/System Improvement Fund to cover the cost of these repairs. This fund was established by Town Meeting in 2020 for the maintenance, repair, and improvement of the water system. A MOTION was made by Selectman Nicolopoulos and seconded by Selectwoman Colby to authorize the withdrawal of $21,002.63 from the Water Capital Replacement/System Improvements fund pursuant to the documents in our packet pages 10-17. MOTION PASSED 3-0. V. CONSENT AGENDA 1.

Utility Billing Warrant - Water A MOTION was made by Selectman Nicolopoulos and duly seconded by Selectwoman Colby to approve the consent agenda as presented. MOTION PASSED 3-0. 3 August 11, 2026 VI. TOWN MANAGER’S REPORT Community Development Master Plan: The Planning Board will be performing a buildout analysis for inclusion in the updated Plan. A build-out analysis is used to estimate and describe the amount and the location of future development that may be allowed to occur within the Town under the current zoning and development regulations. This information is instrumental for estimating future demands on public infrastructure and the environment.

It also provides a glimpse of the Town’s possible future when all the remaining buildable land is developed. Bow Mills Study: A kickoff meeting was held in order to map out the process and discuss what the Town hopes to accomplish. Emergency Management Generators: Director Beaulac is compiling an inventory of all Town emergency generators and will be conducting testing all of them to ensure that they are in working order. Facilities Recreation Center addition: The project has been completed and most materials, supplies and equipment have been moved into the storage areas.

Facilities Manager Chris Andrews and Maintenance Aid Emily Dorman played an integral part in the project including painting, landscaping, re-installation of the watering system and much more. Chris and the contractor did a great job managing the project and keeping the construction cost under the budgeted amount. Municipal Building: New gutters are currently scheduled for installation in mid-September. Finance FY2027-28 Budget: Director Cheryl Linder and I will be meeting with department heads over the new few weeks to have preliminary discussions with them on their budgets including any new personnel or grade changes, equipment needs, etc. Fire Ambulance:

The Department is currently down to one ambulance. The other ambulance continues to have problems with the electrical systems. We have worked hard in-house to make the required repairs but will be taking it to a company specializing in this area. Grants: The Department has submitted an application for a federal “100%” grant for a ventilator. The grant is for up to $25,000. They are working on an application for a grant for the purchase of gear for new hires. Captain Craig Beulac is spearheading these efforts. 4 August 11, 2026 Public Works DOT paving: The State is scheduled to begin conducting grinding and paving operations on August 31.

Pike Industries will be paving Logging Hill Road, Bow Center Road, Logging Hill Road and portions of Bow Bog Road. Town Clerk/Tax Collector Elections: The Town Clerk and other election officials have begun meeting to discuss the upcoming State elections. A new State law requires that the Supervisors of the Checklist purge the checklist and remove any voter who did not vote in the last State/Federal election. Supervisors purging the checklist if they didn’t vote in last State or Federal election. VII. DISCUSSION/ACTION ITEMS 1.

Acceptance of July 14, 2026, Meeting Minutes A MOTION was made by Selectman Nicolopoulos and seconded by Selectwoman Colby to approve the July 14, 2026 meeting minutes as amended. MOTION PASSED 3-0. There was a question on the draft minutes of whether there was a motion made Chair McDaniel confirmed there was a motion and it passed unanimously. 2. Acceptance of DWSRF loan for the Bow Junction Water Loop Project The Board discussed the DWSRF loan and noted for the record that the Board was given authority to enter into an agreement at Town Meeting pending approval from Concord, so there was no need for a motion. 3.

Community Center Boiler The Board reviewed a memo from Facilities Manager Chris Andrews. He is recommending that the Board accept a bid from Bow Plumbing and Heating, in the amount $55,000 to replace the boiler at the Community Center. The company was the lowest bidder of the three (3) bids received. A MOTION was made by Selectman Nicolopoulos and seconded by Selectwoman Colby to accept the bid from Bow Plumbing and Heating in the amount of $55,000 to replace the boiler at the Community Center. MOTION PASSED 3-0. 4. Water Capital Replacement/System Improvements fund Withdrawal Request This was addressed at the beginning of the agenda, while Director Lindner had the floor.

5 August 11, 2026 5. Landfill Solar Project – Update/Recommendation - Zoning Chair McDaniel summarized a recommendation from Town Counsel concerning the landfill solar project. There was a zoning discrepancy with the proposed solar array from Kearsarge Bow LF, LLC whereas the town’s current zoning ordinance imposes a size limitation and because of this a special exception may be required.

Selectwoman Colby moved that, while it is unclear whether a special exception is required for the proposed solar array to be constructed by Kearsarge Bow LF, LLC on the Town’s Landfill Parcel (Tax Map 14-4-71), to the extent that one is required, the Select Board hereby waives Kearsarge Bow LF, LLC’s obligation to obtain such relief under Section 3(A)(i)(2) of the Lease Agreement, as the proposal constitutes a governmental land use pursuant to RSA 674:54. MOTION PASSED 3-0. VIII. REPORTS 1. Board Committee Reports Chair McDaniel gave an update on the Planning Board activities and Selectwoman Colby updated the Board on the Heritage Commission and the 300th Celebration Committee. IX.

BOTTOM LINES Selectman Nicolopoulos: none Selectwoman Colby: The 300th Celebration Committee is looking for suggestions on a place to hold a carnival. Thank you to Darcy Little for all her work with our kids at the Bow Recreation Center and to her team. Chair McDaniel: none Follow up: The Heritage Commission would like to have the Town Manager’s office follow up with the volunteer who wanted to clean cemetery headstones. A gentleman who had missed the Public Comment portion of the meeting asked if he could speak. His name is Jason Gerhard, and he spoke to the Board about the role and responsibilities of Grand Juries in the State of New Hampshire. X.
NON-PUBLIC SESSION RSA 91-A:3, II (e) (none) XI. ADJOURNMENT At 6:42 p.m. A MOTION was made by Selectman Nicolopoulos and duly seconded by Selectwoman Colby to adjourn the meeting. MOTION PASSED 5-0.

Review Project/Task List 21 • Amber Bow Associates – Construction is at least underway for all of the buildings, and several 22 are occupied. One of the four original buildings has been approved for bulk storage of gases for 23 industrial use by Special Exception.

The proposed development may include a warehousing and distribution 34 center, and the possibility of a restaurant/coffee shop. 35 • I 89-Exit 1 – Governor Ayotte vetoed the Ten Year Transportation Improvement Plan.

36 • Water Extension Project to Bow Mills and Bow Junction – The Northern Border Regional 37 Commission grant-funded feasibility study for the Bow Mills area water extension is underway. 38 The Town has selected Resilience Planning and Design as the consultant, and the project kickoff 39 meeting was held last week. The consultant is reviewing existing studies, visiting the Bow Mills 40 area, and gathering background information. The study will include outreach to property owners, 41 the public, and Town boards and committees, and the consultant will likely attend a future BDC 42 meeting to gather input. The anticipated economic development strategy report completion is by 43 Town meeting.

Town of Bow Capital Improvement Committee Ju ly 2 8 , 202 6 Unapproved Minutes The Capital Improvement Program (CIP) Committee met, Tuesday , Ju ly 2 8 , 2026 at 5:30 PM in Room B at the Municipal Building, 10 Grandview Road, Bow, NH. Committee members present: Chair Mark Davis (Citizen Representative ) ( remote), Vice Chair Glenn Dugas (Citizen Representative) , Harry Judd (Citizen Representative) , Jenna Reardon ( Alt. School Board Representative) , Angela Brennan ( Selectboard Representative ) , Jonathan Pietrangelo (Planning Board Representative) , and Jeffrey Knight ( 6:05 PM ) (Budget Committee Representative ) . Absent (excused): Martin Osterloh (School Board Representative) .

Bow Town employees present : Town Manager David Stack , Finance Director Cheryl Lindner , Public Works Director Tim Sweeney, Fleet Manager Dan Snodgrass , Parks and Recreation Director Darcy Little, and Fire Chief Dennis Comeau. I. Call to Order The Vice Chair called the meeting to order at 5:30 P M. II . Approval of Minutes – The minutes of August 11, 2025 , from the previous year’s CIP Committee , were appro ved as submitted. Vice Chair Dugas moved and Harry Judd seconded the motion to approve the minutes of July 23, 2026 . Clarifications and corrections were made by the Committee. Both the motion maker and seconder agreed to the revisions.

A vote was called on the revised minutes which were carried by unanimous vote of the Committee. I II . Department Reviews Parks and Recreation – Director Darcy Little addressed the contribution of $150,000 for the Community Center Project. She stated the program can’t maintain an amount of $150,000 every year . She will have a better idea where finances stand in approximately a month as revenue and expenses come in. Town Manager Stack and Director Little have discussed a “set-aside” or capital reserve fund . She would like to keep $200,000 in reserve for unanticipated circumstances.

Quotes for paving have been coming in high so there was a question whether the inflation rate should be increased . Recreation Center Septic System - The Director will research the age and quality of the sewer system to answer questions from Committee. Hanson Playground Equipment is to come off the summary sheet. Fire Department – Vehicles and Equ i pment. The bidde r chosen to replace Ambulance A-1 (scheduled to be replaced in 2026) has dropped out without notice . T he Fire Department (FD) will now have to locate a new supplier and restart the process of bidding out replacement of Ambulance A-1. The Committee discussed including the condition of the vehicles on the project sheet s .

The Fire Chief considers Ambulance A-1 to be in poor condition. The Committee i s concerned that the FD Capital Reserve F und for equipment is projected to be at a substantial deficit starting 2035/2036 and agreed to add $25,000 to the contribution amount making it $300,000 to start to address the deficit. The inflation rate for both the Pumper E-2 and Utility Truck will be changed from 5% t o 3.5%. Change the estimated life of the ambulances A-1 and A-2 to 9 years. Fire Suppression Water Supply CRF – The Committee wants to have all the dry hydrants (9) included on the summary spreadsheet with footnotes as to their location. Separate them out into categories of steel or concrete.

Chief Comeau will inspect the pipes and list the condition, location and construction material of each one to bring the information to the Committee. Public Works – Equipment. The Utility Service Truck T-71 has 175,000 miles on it and is at the end of its life span . It is scheduled to be replaced in 2027/2028. Change the estimated life span to be 15 years. Directo r Sweeney wants to hold off on the street sweeper and contract the services out for a year while he evaluates whether owning, leasing or contracting is the best option for the town . Move the o ne-ton Utility Truck, T-9 up from 2029/2030 to 2028/2029.

Bridges and Highway – Bow Bog Road Culvert – increas e estimated cost to $800,000 and add footnote that it was approved at 2026 Town Meeting. V. Meeting Dates - The Committee decided to hold the next CIP meeting on August 31, 2026 , 5:30PM in Room B at the Municipal Building covering Facilities, Library and School . V I . Adjourn Upon a motion by Harry Judd and a second by Mark Davis , it was unanimously voted to adjourn the meeting at 7:07 PM. Respectfully submitted Wendy Gilman, Recording Secretary

TOWN OF BOW Planning Board 10 Grandview Road, Bow, New Hampshire 03304 Phone (603) 223-3976 | Fax (603) 225-2982 | Website www.bownh.gov 1 Master Plan Steering Committee Minutes July 14, 2026 The Town of Bow Master Plan Steering Committee met on Tuesday, July 14, 2026 at 6:00 PM in Meeting Room C of the Bow Municipal Building, 10 Grandview Road, Bow, NH. Members Present: Tom O’Donovan, Sandy Crystall, Jill Hadaway, Kristen Hayden, and Nancy Rheinhardt. Others Present: Karri Makinen, Town of Bow Community Development Director; Mike Tardiff, Central NH Regional Planning Commission (CNHRPC) Executive Director;

and Craig Tufts, CNHRPC Senior GIS/Transportation Planner The meeting was called to order at 6:14 PM. • May 19, 2026 Draft Minutes • The Committee reviewed the draft minutes from their previous meeting on May 19, 2026. • A motion was made by Nancy Rheinhardt and seconded by Sandy Crystall to approve the minutes. Vote: 5:0. • Mike Tardiff presented a status update on the project. CNHRPC staff have been working on updates to the Transportation chapter as well as mapping updates.

• Craig Tufts presented a map with proposed changes to street classifications • Karri Makinen explained that the Subdivision Regulations include definitions of the classifications for Arterial, Collector, and Local roads. These classifications represent the functional class of the road. Several other regulations including sight distance requirements for new driveways and lane width, ROW width for new roads vary based on the classification. The classification of some roads in the Master Plan map do not align with the definitions in the Subdivision Regulations, leading to conflicts.

• Craig Tufts pointed out several roads on the map to be changed from local to collector, based on recommendations from the Town Engineer. • There was consensus that White Rock Hill Road should be designated as a Collector rather than Arterial. • Tom O’Donovan proposed that South Bow Road and Bow Bog Road should be Arterial based on the high volumes of cut-through traffic. A conversation followed on whether the classification should reflect intended or actual use. • Vaughn Road will need further review. • Hall Street should be Arterial • The Steering Committee will need to review potential implications of these classification changes before finalizing the map.

• Craig Tufts then presented a map of recent subdivisions from 2020 through 2026. • Karri Makinen commented that adding an annotation for the number of buildable lots created by each subdivision would help add context to the map. Page 2 of 2 • Recent Site Plans will be added to the map as well. • The Committee then reviewed a draft land use map. Craig Tufts led a discussion on the land use codes used. • Committee members will review the map in detail and send any questions/comments to Karri. • Traffic counts were collected; data to be processed. The next meeting was scheduled for August 18, 2026 at 6:00 PM. Nancy Rheinhardt made a motion to adjourn the meeting, seconded by Sandy Crystall.
A unanimous vote in favor followed. Meeting was adjourned at 7:05 PM.

TOWN OF BOW Conservation Commission 10 Grandview Road, Bow, New Hampshire 03304 Phone (603) 223-3970 Fax (603) 225-2982 Website: www.bownh.gov Email: conservation@bownh.gov Conservation Commission Approved Minutes Monday, July 13, 2026 The regular meeting of the Bow Conservation Commission was held on Monday, July 13, 2026, at 7:00 PM in Room C of the Municipal Office Building, 10 Grandview Road. Chair Crystall called the meeting to order at 7:02 PM. Commissioners present: Sandy Crystall, Lisa Lindquist, Mary Farrell, Tom O'Donovan Excused: Dik Dagavarian Other attendees: Ginger Iverson, Recording Secretary 1.

Eversource – Herbicide Notice Chair Crystall reported that this was the first herbicide notification the Town had received from Eversource, which had historically relied on mechanical vegetation management. This work is tentatively scheduled to commence mid-August 2026. She reviewed the information submitted, including right-of-way maps, vegetation management diagrams, and general program information, noting that the materials lacked sufficient detail regarding where herbicides would be applied. Ms. Lindquist expressed concern about treatment areas located near private wells and wetlands. Mr.

O'Donovan suggested requesting additional information describing the proposed application plan, what quantities are being applied, treatment locations, targeted vegetation, and methods. Commissioners discussed concerns regarding drinking water, wetlands, nearby residential wells, public notification, and the need for more detailed information than was provided. Chair Crystall noted that selective herbicide applications may offer habitat benefits compared with broad mechanical clearing but emphasized that questions remained regarding groundwater protection and wetland impacts. Ms. Farrell made a motion, seconded by Ms.

Lindquist, that the Conservation Commission respond to Eversource's June 12, 2026 herbicide notification by stating that it could not support the proposed herbicide program based on the information provided and requesting additional details regarding the proposed herbicide application plan. Vote 4:0. Chair Crystall will submit the Commission's response and seek additional documentation from other Town departments/committees while raising the matter with the Select Board. 2. Robertson Trail – Wetlands Permit Approved: Schedule and Plan for Construction Chair Crystall reported that the Conservation Commission received the state wetlands permit for the Robertson Trail project.

Permit documents have been uploaded to the Commission's shared files Conservation Commission Approved Minutes 07/13/2026 2 and will be posted at the project site during construction. Mr. O'Donovan reported that construction is being planned for the fall and volunteers have already expressed interest. Mr. O'Donovan made a motion, seconded by Ms. Farrell, to authorize expenditure of up to the previously budgeted $4,000 for lumber and hardware associated with the Robertson Trail project now that the permit has been approved. Vote 4:0. Commissioners discussed volunteer scheduling, trail alignment, material delivery, and access during construction.

Lumber will be delivered and transported to the work site by volunteers using smaller vehicles. Chair Crystall noted that two culverts on the trail are deteriorating and a permit trail notification to replace them was approved in 2022. 3. Conservation Land Management Marking Knox Forest Boundary – Chair Crystall reported that Ron Klemarczyk has been asked to mark the Knox Forest boundary behind properties along Knox Road. Addressing Merrill Crossing Issue – Commissioners confirmed that Ron Klemarczyk would contact another surveyor regarding the Merrill Crossing property boundary issue.

Addressing Violations on Town Land/State Easement – Chair Crystall reported discussing violations on Town-owned land under a Fish and Game easement with Code Enforcement Officer Will Dinsmore. Ms. Crystall will provide Mr. Dinsmore with additional information to enable him to prepare and send formal correspondence. Knox Forest – Bittersweet Patch (Old Log Landing) – Commissioners agreed that manual removal of bittersweet is practical and to schedule a volunteer workday for cooler weather. Chair Crystall also reported a Callery pear tree at the site that will require treatment. 4.

Story Maps/Online Maps – Update Chair Crystall reported that the existing Story Map is no longer functioning properly. Maintaining the Story Map as designed requires significant ESRI licensing credits. Craig Tufts of the Regional Planning Commission recommended replacing the existing Story Maps with a single interactive map containing selectable layers. Commissioners agreed this approach would improve usability while reducing licensing costs. Mr. O’Donovan identified the Conservation Focus Areas from the Natural Resources Inventory as the highest priority layer because it is not currently available through the Town GIS.

Other conservation layers are already available elsewhere or could be consolidated. Ms. Crystall will coordinate GIS and Story Map updates with the Regional Planning Commission and Town staff. 5. Land Conservation Work – Status Mr. O'Donovan reported that, consistent with the Commission's previous nonpublic session, the Purchase and Sale Agreement for a pending land conservation project has been signed on behalf of the Commission and will be signed by Bow Open Spaces tomorrow. Following execution by the property owner, the transaction will proceed to the next phase. 6.

VLAP (Volunteer Lake Assessment Program) – Update Conservation Commission Approved Minutes 07/13/2026 3 June Results – Chair Crystall reported that June laboratory results have been received and the July sampling which was attended by the state biologist has been completed. She thanked the volunteers who assisted with sample collection. Ms. Crystall stated that August will be the last of the three sampling events. Funding for VLAP – Chair Crystall reported receiving the first 2026 laboratory invoice and noted that annual program funding had not yet been formally authorized. Mr. O’Donovan made a motion, seconded by Ms.

Farrell, to appropriate $400 for the Town's participation in the Volunteer Lake Assessment Program (VLAP) during calendar year 2026. Vote 4:0. The Commissioners noted the continued elevated chloride concentrations at the Town Pond inlet and possible sources, including road salt from nearby development, such as the Memorial School parking lot. Mr. O’Donovan discussed the wellhead protection area for the Bow municipal water system, two wells on a portion of Route 3-A, and discussed ongoing efforts by the Town's Drinking Water Protection Committee to establish a reduced-salt management area along Route 3A to protect municipal wells. Mr.

O'Donovan reported that the New Hampshire Department of Transportation indicated it would consider a reduced-salt designation if the Town demonstrates broad community support from the Select Board, School District, Police Department, Fire Department, and other stakeholders. Commissioners expressed concern that chloride levels in Town Pond and municipal wells continue to increase. 7. BCC Participation in the 300th Anniversary – Mary Farrell Ms. Farrell reported that planning is underway for Bow's 300th Anniversary, with activities expected to take place throughout the anniversary year. Proposed events include a parade, community celebration, cookout, educational displays, and fireworks.

The Commissioners discussed ways the Conservation Commission could participate in the celebration. Ideas included offering guided walks highlighting Bow's conservation lands, natural resources, wildlife habitat, and environmental history; collaborating with the Heritage Commission and Historical Society; and providing educational displays or information booths during community events. Additional suggestions included interpreting historic mill sites, cellar holes, stone walls, and early settlement features located on conservation properties; highlighting the Robertson Trail, Eagle Trail, Hammond Nature Preserve, and other public conservation lands;

developing educational materials describing changes to Bow's landscape over the past 300 years; and organizing a conservation-themed scavenger hunt or geocaching activity. Several historically significant locations were identified for possible inclusion in anniversary programming, including the former mill site near Route 3-A, the cellar hole along Eagle Trail, and several historic cemeteries throughout town, including Quimby Cemetery and other small family burial grounds. The Commission agreed to continue developing ideas as anniversary planning progresses and requested that the topic remain on future meeting agendas. 8.

Other Items Conservation Commission Approved Minutes 07/13/2026 4 Follow-up on Previous Development Reviews – Mr. O'Donovan requested an update on the previously reviewed solar project and tree-topping proposal. Chair Crystall will verify the approval conditions requiring the applicant to return to the Conservation Commission and Planning Board. Westover Open Space and Boundary Concerns –Mr. O’Donovan reviewed concerns regarding possible encroachment into Town-owned open space associated with recent residential construction. He raised concerns about locating granite boundary monuments. Chair Crystall will coordinate a field inspection with Town staff.

Members also discussed improving boundary marking. Belanger Property – Mr. O'Donovan requested confirmation that removal of a shed within a protected buffer was included as a Planning Board approval condition. Chair Crystall recalled that it was included. She will provide the Planning Board conditions of approval. Upcoming Educational Opportunities – Chair Crystall reviewed upcoming educational programs offered by the New Hampshire Association of Conservation Commissions, including a webinar on proposed wetland rule changes and the Annual Meeting in November. Commissioners expressed interest in attending and agreed to consider funding once registration costs are available.

Nonpublic Session – RSA 91-A:3, II (as needed) – N/A Unapproved Minutes: June 15, 2026 Ms. Lindquist made a motion to approve the June 15, 2026 minutes as amended. The motion was seconded by Ms. Farrell. Vote 4:0. Adjournment Mr. O'Donovan made a motion to adjourn the meeting. The motion was seconded by Ms. Farrell. Vote 4:0. The meeting adjourned at 8:05 p.m. Next meeting: August 17, 2026 Respectfully submitted, Ginger Iverson Recording Secretary

300th Anniversary Celebration Committee Agenda for 07/07/2026, 5:30 PM Bow Municipal Building, 10 Grandview Rd 1)​ Call to Order 2)​ Public Comment 3)​ Meeting Minutes from 3/31/2026 4)​ Treasurer’s Report 5)​ Community Feedback / Poll Results a)​ Facebook b)​ Master Plan Survey 6)​ Updates from other organizations and Town Committees 7)​ Old Home Day schedules from other communities 8)​ Review Brainstorming Sheet 9)​ Election of Officers a)​ Chair b)​ Vice Chair c)​ Secretary d)​ Treasurer 10)​Adjournment Attendance:

Eleana Colby, Selectboard​ ​ ​ Harry Hadaway, Bow Open Spaces David West, Heritage Commission​ ​ Billy Knapp, Bow Budget Committee Mary Farrell, Conservation Commission​ Jason Coache, Resident Kendra Ricard, Heritage Commission Absent: Jared Bland, Bow Athletic Club​ ​ Jennifer Hittle, Resident Andy Foote, Bow Business Development Call to Order: The meeting was called to order by Selectwoman Colby at 5:31 pm Those in attendance introduced themselves and the organizations and committees they are members of. Selectwoman Colby explained that there were absences due to a scheduling conflict with the High School’s Winter Sports Awards Night.

She then provided a handout from the New Hampshire Municipal Association (NHMA) and a brief overview of the “Right to Know Law”. Public Comment: None Objectives/Vision: Selectwoman Colby updated the committee on the 300th Anniversary budget. The current balance of the fund is $12,476.16, with an anticipated deposit of $10,000 on July 1, 2026, as approved in the 2026/2027 Town Budget. The committee discussed possible events, the length of the celebration, timelines to consider, and the date of the original charter. Mrs. Ricard noted that the date of the original charter's signing remains unclear; however, we do know it was in May of 1727.

The committee informally agreed that a large scale event should be held sometime in May of 2027. Mr. West offered information regarding the 250th and 275th anniversary celebrations, noting that the 250th was a week long and the 275th just one day. The committee discussed the possibility of hosting 3 months of various activities from April to June, before school closes for the summer. No formal vote was taken. Mr. West and Mrs. Ricard also discussed the time capsule, which was buried during the 250th celebration, dug up during library renovations, and is sitting unopened in the library. It was suggested that the committee incorporate opening the capsule and possibly burying a new one. Mr.

Coach mentioned this would be a great opportunity to get the schools and students involved. The committee added to their brainstorming sheet of ideas for fundraising, events, other boards, organizations to contact, town departments and resources, and past commemorative merchandise, including the coins that were purchased years ago and to be sold for the 300th Anniversary Celebration. Selectwoman Colby will be following up with the Town Manager and Selectboard for more details on pricing, metal types, design, and quantity. Fireworks and a Parade were mentioned around a Memorial Day discussion.

The committee informally agreed that these two events would be strong possibilities, but would be interested in hosting fireworks in a different location than the town fields, as they are concerned about parking and viewing. Structure/Elections: A motion was made by Mary Farrell and seconded by Mr. Knapp to table the discussion and election of Chair, Vice Chair, and Secretary until more members are present.

Motion Passes 7-0-0​ Selectwoman Colby asked that each member seek information from their respective groups and committees regarding what events they may want to host, either from their own list of ideas or from ideas generated by this committee, and bring any ideas back to the committee at the next meeting. The meeting was adjourned

HOUSEHOLD HAZARDOUS WASTE DAY October 17, 2026 Sherri led a discussion on options for addressing the items previously disposed of by Woody Bowne given that he is no longer working as the Supervisor of the Dunbarton transfer station. He had previously rented a U-Haul and coordinated disposal of multiple items from HHWD including batteries, light bulbs, propane tanks, Helium tanks, and fire extinguishers through North Coast Services, (now TerraCycle), located at 44 Locke Road, Concord NH. Sherri reported that she spoke with North Coast and they told her they can collect these items directly from us the Monday after HHWD for a $125 fee.

Additionally, Irene spoke with Greg Rule, Interim Manager at the Dunbarton Transfer Station, who stated that he should be able to arrange the disposal of these items as well. Irene emailed Mr. Rule the list of items and fees from last year and asked him to confirm, but has not heard back from him yet. Sherri also spoke with TIm Sweeney from Bow’s Public Works Department and he would prefer not to transport these recyclables directly to North Coast. Irene will follow up with both Greg Rule and North Coast to confirm that both options are available to us. It was decided the committee will make a final decision on which option to utilize at the next meeting.

Sherri updated that she is working on the contract between the Town of Bow and NH Recycles which has agreed to be our vendor for HHWD again this year. Sherri made a motion that we will require identification at HHWD this year to ensure participants are residents of Bow and Dunbarton. It was seconded by Deb Unger and unanimously approved. 7. Trex Program: Plastic bag and Film Collection Members have continued to weigh bags and upload pictures and weights since the last meeting. Given the hassle and recent changes to the rewards program, it was agreed that we will stop weighing and uploading pictures of weights for now since we have already received our allotted annual gift.

We will plan to restart again in April 2027 when we can begin working towards our next annual $100 gift. The free bags we received from the awards program are 55 gallon bags and are too small to use in the Trex bins. However, they can be used for the library bins and to package items. 8.​ HELPSY Helpsy collected 196 pounds in May. 9. Other business Deb is working on an article for the Bow Times for August to provide education on local options for disposing of hard-to-recycle items such as electronics, lightbulbs, and batteries as an alternative to HHWD. She will also post this information on our Facebook page.

Sherri will plan to submit an article to the Bow TImes in September on the topic of “How HHWD keeps our water clean.” Next Committee meeting is September 1, 2026. Meeting adjourned 7:55 p.m. Respectfully Submitted, Irene Hou

The 217 compound is designed to collocate at least four commercial wireless carriers, accessed via a 12- 218 foot wide gravel driveway built with a double-vehicle turnaround on the leased property. Traffic 219 would be typically limited to twice a month per carrier by a pick-up truck or SUV-type vehicle. 220 He discussed the cabinets that would be within the compound.

Utilities will run above-ground 221 via the 12 foot wide access way. 222 Attorney Grossman described Mariner's role as an independent infrastructure provider that has 223 relationship with various carriers. He described that the search for a location included 224 information in the town's study. The tower will provide coverage to South Bow Road, Quimby 225 Road, Woodhill-Hooksett Road, Nottingcook Forest and those in the area, and increase coverage 226 to approximately 1,000 people. 227 Mr. Grossman went on to review data detailing wireless data statistics and trends.

Selectman 228 McDaniel directed the presentation away from broad national policy statistics, emphasizing that 229 the Board's scope is strictly limited to local zoning ordinance alignment rather than national 230 telecom trends or policy issues. 231 Mr. Grossman reviewed the project's consistency with the town ordinance, FAA regulations, 232 FCC regulations, NEPA, and Section 106, historic program review. NH State Historic 233 Preservation Office issued a finding of "no adverse effect". The location avoid impacts to 234 environmentally sensitive area, including wetlands and wetland buffers.

A formal waiver is requested from the 244 tower camouflage regulations, arguing that artificial branching would draw more negative visual 245 attention than a clean lattice design. Chair Sandy Crystall called the meeting to order at 7:04 PM. Commissioners present: Sandy Crystall, Lisa Lindquist, Mary Farrell, Tom O’Donovan, Dik Dagavarian. Other attendees: Ginger Iverson, Recording Secretary 1. Application no. 404-26:

Kearsarge Bow LF LLC – Proposed Wetland CUP to impact approximately 800 sq. ft. of wetland buﬀer for the installation of portions of a ground-mounted solar array. Location: 8 Falcon Way. Map 14, Block 4, Lot 71. Alex Young and Mike Lotti of Kearsarge Energy, along with Marissa Sewell and Rob Bukowski of Weston & Sampson, presented the application following a site walk conducted earlier today. The applicant reviewed the project's history, noting it originated from the Town's 2023 request for proposals and has since advanced through execution of a lease agreement benefiting the Town and School District and securing utility interconnection approval.

Discussion centered on the potential removal of trees creating shade on the proposed solar array. The applicant stated the project could proceed without immediate tree removal and that such work was not necessary for construction. Mr. Young had mentioned the application of 309.02 and Mr. O’Donovan questioned whether any trees proposed for removal were within the wetland boundary. Mr. Young read the language in the rule that describes that harvesting trees in a wetland is allowable under state requirements as long as the stumps will remain. Although the area may change from a forested to a shrub wetland, the wetland itself will not be eliminated.

The applicant indicated that only one or two trees may be located within the delineated wetland, with most removals likely occurring in adjacent uplands. A question had been asked on the site walk about the possibility of topping the pine trees, rather than removing them. Chair Crystall asked Town Forester Ron Klemarczyk, who was present for another item on the agenda, about it. Mr. Klemarczyk advised against topping pine trees, as that creates opportunities for decay of the tree and encourages branching out, which could contribute to blowdowns. He recommended complete removal as needed.

He cautioned that removing the "wind-firm" perimeter trees could increase the risk of blowdown of trees remaining behind them. In response to an inquiry from Mr. O’Donovan and Ms. Lindquist, Mr. Young estimated that retaining the trees could reduce first-year revenue by approximately $25,000 and result in an estimated twenty-year lost revenue of about $640,000. Commissioners requested additional Conservation Commission Approved Minutes 06/15/2026 2 information regarding the projected income and economic effects. Mr. Young stated that the town’s benefits are coming from lease revenue and electricity bill savings.

In extreme shading cases, they would consider making the system smaller, although that was likely not the case here. The applicant anticipated construction beginning in mid to late July and concluding before Thanksgiving, noting that any tree work would ideally occur before the school year. Commissioners also raised concerns regarding wildlife habitat. Several commissioners questioned the relationship of the tree removal relationship to the CUP under review. Chair Crystall responded that the solar panels are within the prime wetland buffer, and thus the wetland CUP is required. She described that beyond the Wetland CUP, the project is subject to site plan approval by the Planning Board.

She noted that tree cutting in the proposed location is not a prime wetland issue. Commissioners agreed that the solar panels in the prime wetland buffer posed minimal environmental impact due to its location on previously disturbed land. The applicant asked about returning to the Conservation Commission with additional information on the tree cutting, as well as the economic information. Ms. Lindquist raised concerns about the visual impacts of the tree removal. The applicants noted that they would be focusing on the tallest pine trees. They would not touch anything from the edge of the road 35 feet in, except the very tall pines. Ms.

Lindquist noted that the application did not have the area of wetland buffer impact noted on the application form. Discussion about habitat impacts, Chair Crystall displayed the aerial image of the landfill area with a lot of pine trees nearby, to show that there are significant amount of pine trees in the adjacent area. Ms. Crystall mentioned the concern is that the wetland area doesn't get disturbed. A motion was made by Mr. Dagavarian and seconded by Mr. O'Donovan to recommend approval of Application #404-26:

Kearsarge Bow LF LLC – Proposed Wetland Conditional Use Permit for the approximately 800 square feet of wetland buffer impact associated with installation of the solar array on the existing landfill cap. The motion carried with a 4:0:1 Vote with Chair Crystall abstaining. Following approval, the Commission reiterated that the applicant return with additional information regarding the proposed tree removal, identification of trees proposed for removal, and descriptions of removal methods, and detailed economic analysis. Mr. Young suggested providing the number of trees and the height criteria for removal/cutting.

They could commit to a tree removal plan that addresses how the trees will be removed. As a result of his experience, Mr. Klemarczyk recommended public outreach to explain the reasons for the tree work and the benefits of the solar project. Robertson Trail Chair Crystall reported that the Conservation Commission had received an email regarding a potentially illegal sign observed near the old log landing, where a trail branches to the left. She noted that the sign is believed to be located on Town-owned property. Klemarczyk stated that he would identify and mark the Knox property boundary behind the houses on Knox Road. 2. Chair Sandy Crystall called the meeting to order at 7:04 PM. Commissioners present: Sandy Crystall, Lisa Lindquist, Mary Farrell, Tom O’Donovan, Dik Dagavarian. Other attendees: Ginger Iverson, Recording Secretary 1. Application no. 404-26:

Kearsarge Bow LF LLC – Proposed Wetland CUP to impact approximately 800 sq. ft. of wetland buﬀer for the installation of portions of a ground-mounted solar array. Location: 8 Falcon Way. Map 14, Block 4, Lot 71. Alex Young and Mike Lotti of Kearsarge Energy, along with Marissa Sewell and Rob Bukowski of Weston & Sampson, presented the application following a site walk conducted earlier today. The applicant reviewed the project's history, noting it originated from the Town's 2023 request for proposals and has since advanced through execution of a lease agreement benefiting the Town and School District and securing utility interconnection approval.

Discussion centered on the potential removal of trees creating shade on the proposed solar array. The applicant stated the project could proceed without immediate tree removal and that such work was not necessary for construction. Mr. Young had mentioned the application of 309.02 and Mr. O’Donovan questioned whether any trees proposed for removal were within the wetland boundary. Mr. Young read the language in the rule that describes that harvesting trees in a wetland is allowable under state requirements as long as the stumps will remain. Although the area may change from a forested to a shrub wetland, the wetland itself will not be eliminated.

The applicant indicated that only one or two trees may be located within the delineated wetland, with most removals likely occurring in adjacent uplands. A question had been asked on the site walk about the possibility of topping the pine trees, rather than removing them. Chair Crystall asked Town Forester Ron Klemarczyk, who was present for another item on the agenda, about it. Mr. Klemarczyk advised against topping pine trees, as that creates opportunities for decay of the tree and encourages branching out, which could contribute to blowdowns. He recommended complete removal as needed.

He cautioned that removing the "wind-firm" perimeter trees could increase the risk of blowdown of trees remaining behind them. In response to an inquiry from Mr. O’Donovan and Ms. Lindquist, Mr. Young estimated that retaining the trees could reduce first-year revenue by approximately $25,000 and result in an estimated twenty-year lost revenue of about $640,000. Commissioners requested additional Conservation Commission Approved Minutes 06/15/2026 2 information regarding the projected income and economic effects. Mr. Young stated that the town’s benefits are coming from lease revenue and electricity bill savings.

In extreme shading cases, they would consider making the system smaller, although that was likely not the case here. The applicant anticipated construction beginning in mid to late July and concluding before Thanksgiving, noting that any tree work would ideally occur before the school year. Commissioners also raised concerns regarding wildlife habitat. Several commissioners questioned the relationship of the tree removal relationship to the CUP under review. Chair Crystall responded that the solar panels are within the prime wetland buffer, and thus the wetland CUP is required. She described that beyond the Wetland CUP, the project is subject to site plan approval by the Planning Board.

She noted that tree cutting in the proposed location is not a prime wetland issue. Commissioners agreed that the solar panels in the prime wetland buffer posed minimal environmental impact due to its location on previously disturbed land. The applicant asked about returning to the Conservation Commission with additional information on the tree cutting, as well as the economic information. Ms. Lindquist raised concerns about the visual impacts of the tree removal. The applicants noted that they would be focusing on the tallest pine trees. They would not touch anything from the edge of the road 35 feet in, except the very tall pines. Ms.

Lindquist noted that the application did not have the area of wetland buffer impact noted on the application form. Discussion about habitat impacts, Chair Crystall displayed the aerial image of the landfill area with a lot of pine trees nearby, to show that there are significant amount of pine trees in the adjacent area. Ms. Crystall mentioned the concern is that the wetland area doesn't get disturbed. A motion was made by Mr. Dagavarian and seconded by Mr. O'Donovan to recommend approval of Application #404-26:

Kearsarge Bow LF LLC – Proposed Wetland Conditional Use Permit for the approximately 800 square feet of wetland buffer impact associated with installation of the solar array on the existing landfill cap. The motion carried with a 4:0:1 Vote with Chair Crystall abstaining. Following approval, the Commission reiterated that the applicant return with additional information regarding the proposed tree removal, identification of trees proposed for removal, and descriptions of removal methods, and detailed economic analysis. Mr. Young suggested providing the number of trees and the height criteria for removal/cutting.

They could commit to a tree removal plan that addresses how the trees will be removed. As a result of his experience, Mr. Klemarczyk recommended public outreach to explain the reasons for the tree work and the benefits of the solar project. BOW HERITAGE COMMISSION June 9th, 2026 Meeting minutes Call to Order - 9am GUESTS - Kay Herrick and Candy Ricard GENERAL BUSINESS - Attendance - Eric Anderson, Chair; Sue Wheeler, Secretary, Jim Dimick, John Urdi, Don Fournier, Dave West and Dave Lindquist. Absent are Dik Dagavarian and Select Board representative Eleana Colby. Minutes - Minutes are tabled due to computer issues. Sorry. BHC Financials - In the OB the $750 has been expended. In the HF there was $75 in monthly interest with a total of $23,143.87. Also $551.00 was expended for the gallery system. There was $10.00 in revenue as well. John Urdi asks the BHC where the money came from in our HF?

Some money is ear-marked for certain things and the rest is roll-over from what we didn’t spend from our OB. BHC Out of Pocket expenses - For photo paper, ink and 12 frames for our lower level exhibit the total came to $93.25. John makes a motion to expend the $93.25 from the HF to cover the cost of the supplies. Jim seconds the motion. Ayes have it, 6 to 0. Motion passes. CORRESPONDENCE - Zoning Board/Planning board requests - None at this time. Preservation Easements for Historic Agricultural Structures - The Woodbury barn has been re-applied for this easement for another 10 years. John Urdi got ahold of Barb Lawler and gave her more information for a preservation easement.

He also tried to contact the owners at Leary’s barn on Brown Hill Road. Dave West gave us the news that the old mill site on Route 3-A doesn’t appear to have access to the mill as stated before by this owner. They are still working on the building as well. Eric will check with the building inspector. Kathy Houghton email - The family wanted to hold off sharing the photos with the BHC. She sent 3 photos via email to Eric but the quality was not very good to replicate. She asked about a scanner and Eric graciously sent her the information about ours. Kathy appreciates the email from Eric regarding the scanner.

OLD BUSINESS - NH State Register of Historic Places - Sue will reach out to Judith Goodnow (about the OTH) and Megan to start the process of the application. National Register of Historic Places - Dave W. heard from Megan Rupnik and was told he has to work through an approved consultant. These consultants are from all over the NE area. There are 2 from NH. The consultant reaches out to the NH Cultural resources. The consultants from our area are from Portsmouth and the Lakes region. Dave W. isn’t sure if there is a fee for this process and/or how much it would cost.

Even yet, if the BBMH were on the National Historic register the town could still sell the building.(Boo!) BHC Lower level update - Eric believes that the lower level is getting beautifully set up. Open House time? Jim says we have plenty of availability to have an Open House. John asks if the photos will be archived? Yes, probably so. Jim states that we ought to have a tab up on the website of our room. Named Bow Heritage Room at the Municipal Building. Publication Pieces for the Bow Times - Unfortunately Cheryl M. is not available today.

BHC Historic interview equipment - The question is, is it worthwhile buying the equipment for us or having Connor and Liam do the filming of the interviews? The camera would cost $1124.17. If we ask for video documentation from them would it be seen as a volunteering effort? John will reach out to Connor and see if we get any more information regarding interviewing. NEW BUSINESS - Select Board report - Tabled. Town’s 300th Anniversary - No more meetings have been scheduled. 2026 Bow Heritage Day Event - Need to discuss the details of when, and what, etc. Refreshing of the BCSH and Town Pound - Since there is no electricity at the schoolhouse, we would have to contact Chris for our generator.

Is there any more to do to fix/paint the windows at the schoolhouse? IMPORTANT DATES - BHC Meeting schedule - August 11, 2026 from 9-11am Room C, at the municipal bldg. No Heritage meeting in July. September 10th - Bow Volunteer Appreciation BBQ at the OTH from 5:30 - 7pm. September ?? - BHC to brief the BoS on the Commission’s 2026 activities to date. Work sessions - between June 9th and August 11th, Tues. & Fridays 9 - 12. BURNING ISSUES - There was a gentleman by the name of Steve Leighton (lives across the street from the Observation Tower on Bow Bog) that is inquisitive of knowing more about the structure.

Apparently the dwelling is uninhabited at this point and the relatives aren’t sure what to do with the place. John states that Logging Hill Road will be eventually developed once again. Photos done now to document before anything gets built or changes? And he also asks when the lighting is getting done downstairs in the lower level? We heard prior that usually when schools, etc., were out of session is when they have the time to address the new lighting. Dave L. asks if the small farming tools are here at the BHC room? The voting booth is still there at the schoolhouse. We ought to check the books there and go through them and see if we want to bring extras over to the BHC room.

Sue has brought her glass negatives to Ever Present in Manchester to have developed in a thumb drive. Waiting on the results. Candy & Kay talked to Karen Blanchard Mitchell and Karen says she wants to start cleaning out. Candy told her NOT to throw away any Bow related things. Jim tells us a story (true) about when he worked for the Phone Co. in 1980 there was a fire in the generator room of Garvins Falls. The boss needed the phone to work! Jim goes through the entrance door and the police are saying, Leave!! The fire marshall has not shown up yet and Jim quickly takes action and cuts the phone lines. But, the phone in the maintenance room still worked. Yay!

The guy was thrilled and Jim saved the day. ADJOURNMENT - Jim makes a motion to adjourn with Dave W. seconding the motion. Ayes have it in favor to adjourn at 10:45, 7 to 0. Motion passes Respectfully submitted, Sue Wheeler, Secretary BHC
