TOWN OF BOW TRUSTEE OF TRUST FUNDS MINUTES January 29, 2026 APPROVED Jon Marvin called the meeting to order at 8:40 AM. Present: Trustees Jon Marvin, Mary Beth Walz and Kate Young, Cambridge Trust Company Representatives Lisa Tourangeau and Brian Bickford Minutes: Review and approval of the October 30, 2025 minutes. New Business: Mr. Bickford provided an overview of the investment markets. Equity performed well in 2025 so overall a very good year with international equities a big driver of equity returns. While tech stocks had another good year there was broadening out of returns over the course of the year.

The S & P went from being just shy of a 20% correction in April to finish the year up almost 16%. Inflation is slowly decreasing but has not come down to the Fed’s desired rate of 2% and labor demand is stabilizing into a low hiring/low firing environment. International performance was helped by the dollar weakening, an increase in European defense spending and attractive valuations. Cambridge feels the dollar will continue to weaken which is positive for international investments. There is a general thought that the economy will experience a positive fiscal stimulus in the first half of the year as a result of impact of the One Big Beautiful Bill;

mostly due to individual and corporate tax cuts. The Fed decreased rates three times last year but the expectation is for only two cuts this year and the first one may not be until June. Interest rates have come down which has helped fixed income returns since as yields come down prices go up. The Capital Reserve account allocation was 85% fixed income and 15% cash as 12/31/25 so very similar to the allocation at the end of September. The total return for the past year was 5.1% which is close to the benchmark (5.9%) for the year.

As noted in previous meetings it is tough to beat the benchmark as the benchmark allows for lower fixed income credit risk (down to BBB) then Investment Policy Statement allows. The average credit quality (AA) of the Capital Reserve portfolio remains better than the benchmark. The current Yield to Maturity (YTM) is 3.7% and the average duration for Capital Reserve funds is 2.18 years (basically the same as last September). Fixed income with a market value of a around $1.6 million matures in 2026 with over half having very low coupon rates so will arguably be able to re-invest and get better coupon rates. 77% of the account allocation is in government fixed income.

The Trust Fund account was up 10.35% for 2025 so the performance remains generally better than the benchmarks. The current allocation is 31% in equities with 80% of that allocation invested in domestic equity funds and 20% in international. Mr. Bickford asked if the town anticipated any income needs in the near future so Mr. Marvin said he would reach out to the Town Finance Director. Lastly there was a discussion regarding the Investment Policy Statement guidelines and the issue of credit ratings limit as regards the purchased of fixed income.

It was decided that the current rating limits were overly restrictive so the Trustees voted to revise the credit ratings range to allow for investments with ratings of A- or A3. The revised IPS will be signed by the Trustees and forwarded onto Cambridge. There being no further business to bring before the Board, the meeting was adjourned at 9:25 AM.

Based on the test 97 pit results, he testified that the area contains shallow soils, ledge close to the surface, exposed 98 bedrock, and poorly drained soils, and lacks a suitable receiving layer necessary for installation 99 of an on-site septic system. Wechsler noted that he reviewed the historic subdivision plan, current survey data, and other 126 project documentation. He noted that efforts to avoid impacts to the wetland buffer would still require 137 grading to extend into the future road widening area and the right-of-way. He stated that 138 accommodating a residence in the frontage area would also require encroachment into the 139 wetland buffer.

140 141 He further stated that an access driveway to the rear of the property has already received wetland 142 crossing approval and that, regardless of where a residence is located, some form of driveway 143 access to the upland portion of the lot would be required. He noted that construction in the 144 frontage area would constitute an additional impact beyond the driveway and would not be 145 consistent with conditional use permit standards requiring minimization of impacts to the 146 wetland buffer. 147 148 Based on these constraints, Mr.

Wechsler testified that he was unable to design a compliant 149 layout for development in the frontage area and stated that development in the rear portion of the 150 property, as originally proposed, was more feasible. 151 152 Mr. McDaniel noted that Ms. Panciocco requested the rehearing be limited to Condition #3 of 153 the approval and not include discussion of the driveway. The Board agreed to confine discussion 154 and testimony to the scope of Condition #3 and requested that all parties respect those limits 155 during the hearing. 156 157 Ms. Panciocco asked Mr. Wechsler if he thought NHDES would grant waivers for the minimum 158 soil separation requirements. Mr.

Wechsler noted that, even if waivers were sought, he did not 159 believe NHDES would grant waivers for the minimum soil separation requirements. He noted his 160 professional background, including prior employment with NHDES and approximately 19 years 161 of experience designing septic systems, and stated he has never seen such waivers issued for 162 these conditions. 163 164 Mr. Wechsler stated that based on test pit data alone, the frontage area cannot support a 165 compliant septic system for residential use. He concluded that development in the frontage area 166 is not feasible under existing regulatory standards. 167 168 Mr.

McDaniel asked if the applicant’s consultants had explored whether allowing development 169 within the wetland buffer through a Conditional Use Permit (CUP) would enable installation of a 170 septic system in the frontage area. 171 172 Mr. Wechsler responded that this option was evaluated during site layout analysis. Test pits conducted both 175 within and beyond the originally designated area did not achieve the minimum 18 inches of 176 natural soil over ledge.

TOWN OF BOW Conservation Commission 10 Grandview Road, Bow, New Hampshire 03304 Phone (603) 223-3970 Fax (603) 225-2982 Website: www.bownh.gov Email: conservation@bownh.gov Conservation Commission Approved Minutes Monday, January 12, 2026 The regular meeting of the Bow Conservation Commission was held on Monday, January 12, 2026 at 7:00 PM in Room C of the Municipal Office building at 10 Grandview Road. Chair Sandy Crystall called the meeting to order at 7:04 PM. Members present: Sandy Crystall, Lisa Lindquist, Dik Dagavarian, Mary Farrell, and Tom O’Donovan (via telephone). Other attendees: Ginger Iverson, Recording Secretary. Mr.

O’Donovan stated that he could not attend the meeting in person as he was out of town. Ms. Lindquist made a motion to allow Mr. O’Donovan to participate remotely due to his being out of town in accordance with RSA 91-A:2, III. The motion was seconded by Ms. Farrell. Vote 4:0:1 and approved by roll call vote with Mr. O’Donovan abstaining. 1. Robertson Trail – Functional Assessment Ms. Crystall stated that the contract for the Robertson Trail functional assessment was signed and submitted. The cost was $750. Results are expected within approximately 30 days. Additional application details will be discussed at a future meeting. 2.

Legislation Review The Commission reviewed relevant legislation using NHACC resources. Commission members were encouraged to submit individual positions on bills as desired. Upcoming/public hearings noted for: HB 1600 (Battery Recycling Stewardship Program) – Jan. 20, 2026; HB 1530 (Beaver Dam Notification Bill) – Jan. 14, 2026 and HB 1655 (Funding for state-owned dam maintenance via waterfront fees) – Jan. 21, 2026. Discussion included beaver dam notifications, exemptions for emergencies, fiscal note considerations, and use of beaver flow devices. It was noted that at least two organizations have partial grant funding available for beaver flow device installation. Ms.

Crystall asked the Commissioners for any input for testimony to support the bill. At 7:12 p.m. Mr. O’Donovan exited the meeting [the call was dropped]. Ms. Lindquist made a motion authorizing Chair Crystall to provide testimony on HB 1530 on behalf of the Conservation Commission. The motion was seconded by Ms. Farrell. Vote: 4:0. Chair Crystall mentioned the recently held webinar about how to provide input on proposed legislation. She will check to see if the recording is available. Conservation Commission Approved Minutes 01/12/2026 2 3. Land Conservation Work - Status The property closing was completed successfully on the Ferry Road Conservation Land and the deed was recorded.

The next steps include drafting a press release, planning public access, parking, kiosk placement, and signage. Chair Crystall noted the historical significance (Robinson’s Ferry) and has contacted the Heritage Commission for interpretive input. Additionally there was a discussion about Bow Open Spaces and the Conservation Commission sending a potential outreach letter to a landowner along the Dunbarton boundary for future conservation opportunities. 4. Master Plan Chair Crystall reviewed the draft conservation lands map. She identified the need to clearly distinguish the conservation land, Town-owned land and Town forests. Chair Crystall noted a missing parcel and boundary inconsistencies;

shapefiles will be updated. She requested that Commission members review maps and provide feedback before the January 27, 2026 Master Plan Steering Committee meeting. 5. Project Review Table Chair Crystall noted that the Commission's website is outdated and added this to the project review table as a medium-priority project. Commission members volunteered to review specific sections including conservation lands (Mr. Dagavarian), maps (Ms. Lindquist), links of interest (Ms. Farrell) and a new trails page (Ms. Lindquist). The goals include fixing broken links, updating maps (including Wildlife Action Plan 2025), and adding educational content (e.g., beaver information).

Chair Crystall discussed the need for outreach on wetland buffers, conservation land signage and boundary markers, trail inventory improvements and possible use of trail counters, and review and correction of prime wetland buffer boundaries with NHDES. Chair Crystall added that the project tracking document could be converted to Excel for easier sorting. 6. Other, including Planning Board Projects, NHANRS & Turee Pond The Woetzel/Lehrmann property application was remanded from the Housing Appeals Board and there will be a Planning Board rehearing on January 22. A NHDES Forestry Statutory Permit by Notification was filed for the property.

Chair Crystall noted that there were social media comments targeting Commission members and that Town officials were notified. Other development /wetlands permitting activities discussed were regarding Logging Hill Road, South Street and Dunbarton Center Road. The NHANRS Annual Conference is scheduled for January 30, 2026. Cost to attend is $120/person. Turee Pond – Bow was awarded a 50% grant for diver-assisted suction harvesting for milfoil in Turee Pond. Conservation Commission Approved Minutes 01/12/2026 3 Non-Public Session – RSA 91—A (N/A) Unapproved Minutes: December 15, 2025 Mr. Dagavarian made a motion to approve the December 15, 2025 minutes as amended.

The motion was seconded by Ms. Farrell. Vote 4:0. Adjournment Ms. Lindquist made a motion to adjourn the meeting. The motion was seconded by Ms. Farrell. Vote 4:0. The meeting adjourned at 8:16 p.m. Next meeting: February 9, 2026 Respectfully submitted, Ginger Iverson, Recording Secretary

TOWN OF BOW Planning Board 10 Grandview Road, Bow, New Hampshire 03304 Phone (603) 223-3970 | Fax (603) 225-2982 | Website www.bownh.gov 2026 Proposed Zoning Amendments Voter Guide A. Are you in favor of the adoption of ZONING AMENDMENT A as proposed by the Planning Board vote of January 8, 2026 to amend Section 4.01(B) to remove purpose statements for the overlay districts. And to add the purpose statements for the Wetlands Conservation District to 10.01(A), to add the purpose statements for the Floodplain District to 10.02(A), and to add the purpose statements for the Aquifer Protection District to 10.03(A).

Additionally, to update references to the purpose statements in Sections 10.01(B), 10.02(B), and 10.03(B)? The amendment has been on file at the Municipal Building since December 26, 2025. (Recommended by the Planning Board by a vote of 7-0) This amendment removes purpose statements for the overlay districts out of Article 4 and relocates them to their corresponding sections in Article 10. The purpose statements themselves remain unchanged; the only change is to their location in the ordinance. B.

Are you in favor of the adoption of ZONING AMENDMENT B as proposed by the Planning Board vote of December 18, 2025 to amend Section 5.07 to allow the Planning Board to establish a Site Review Committee for review of minor site plans? The amendment has been on file at the Municipal Building since December 5, 2025. (Recommended by the Planning Board by a vote of 5-0) This amendment allows the Planning Board to establish a Site Review Committee which would review minor site plans.

If authorized and the Planning Board chooses to establish such a committee, the Planning Board will need to specify application, acceptance and approval procedures and define what types of site plans would be eligible for review by the Site Review Committee. The Planning Board would then hold a public hearing to amend the Site Plan Review Regulations to make these changes. C.

Are you in favor of the adoption of ZONING AMENDMENT C as proposed by the Planning Board vote of January 8, 2026 to amend Section 5.11, Table of Use Regulations, to add multi-family housing as a permitted use in the Commercial District and to add Section 7.28 regarding supplemental regulations for multi-family housing in the Commercial District? The amendment has been on file at the Municipal Building since December 26, 2025. (Recommended by the Planning Board by a vote of 7-0) This amendment is proposed in accordance with RSA 674:80 which permits multi-family residential development in commercially-zoned areas, provided that adequate infrastructure is available.

TOWN OF BOW Planning Board 10 Grandview Road, Bow, New Hampshire 03304 Phone (603) 223-3970 | Fax (603) 225-2982 | Website www.bownh.gov D. Are you in favor of the adoption of ZONING AMENDMENT D as proposed by the Planning Board vote of December 18, 2025 to amend Section 6.02 to clarify that minimum lot frontage must be along a Class V or better road? The amendment has been on file at the Municipal Building since December 5, 2025. (Recommended by the Planning Board by a vote of 5-0) This amendment is a clarification that minimum lot frontage must be on a Class V or better road (not a Class VI road). This concept is already specified in the definition of “frontage” in Article 3;

this amendment reiterates this in Article 6 to provide additional clarity in the section on Minimum Lot Frontage. E. Are you in favor of the adoption of ZONING AMENDMENT E as proposed by the Planning Board vote of January 8, 2026 to amend Section 7.04 regarding Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) to update definitions, to remove the requirement for a Conditional Use Permit for detached Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs), to allow one ADU to be built on any lot with a single-family dwelling, to clarify and to add a clause regarding ADUs in existing non- conforming structures? The amendment has been on file at the Municipal Building since December 26, 2025.

(Recommended by the Planning Board by a vote of 7-0) This amendment is proposed in accordance with RSAs 674:71 to :73 which now allows one Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) on any single-family residential lot, provided that adequate provisions can be made for water and septic. This means that a Conditional Use Permit will no longer be required for detached ADUs. ADUs are also permitted in existing non-conforming structures. F.

Are you in favor of the adoption of ZONING AMENDMENT F as proposed by the Planning Board vote of January 8, 2026 to amend Section 10.01 to remove an applicant’s alternative method for resolving a wetland boundary dispute and to make various other clarifications and corrections? The amendment has been on file at the Municipal Building since December 26, 2025. (Recommended by the Planning Board by a vote of 7-0) This amendment changes the way wetland boundary disputes are handled. If the Planning Board disputes the wetland boundary determined by an applicant’s wetland scientist, the Planning Board may engage a third-party wetland scientist at the applicant’s expense.

The proposed amendment would eliminate an alternative procedure allowing the applicant to retain an additional wetland scientist instead. TOWN OF BOW Planning Board 10 Grandview Road, Bow, New Hampshire 03304 Phone (603) 223-3970 | Fax (603) 225-2982 | Website www.bownh.gov Additional edits in this section are intended provide clarity and consistency. G. Are you in favor of the adoption of ZONING AMENDMENT G as proposed by the Planning Board vote of December 18, 2025 to amend Section 10.03 to update the current edition of the NH Stormwater Manual? The amendment has been on file at the Municipal Building since December 5, 2025.

(Recommended by the Planning Board by a vote of 5-0) This amendment simply updates the reference to reflect the current edition of the NH Stormwater Manual. H. Are you in favor of the adoption of ZONING AMENDMENT H as proposed by the Planning Board vote of December 18, 2025 to amend Section 11.04 to add subsection H, Adaptive Reuse, related to repurposing existing buildings for residential use? The amendment has been on file at the Municipal Building since December 5, 2025.

(Recommended by the Planning Board by a vote of 5-0) This amendment is proposed in accordance with RSA 674:80 which permits existing buildings to be repurposed for adaptive reuse for residential purposes without conforming to current setbacks, height, or frontage requirements, provided that the building’s floor area, height, and setbacks do not change. I.

Are you in favor of the adoption of ZONING AMENDMENT I as proposed by the Planning Board vote of January 8, 2026 to amend the expiration time period for excavation permits in Section 14.05(B) from two years to not more than five years, correlating with the progress plan update requirement specified in the NH Department of Environmental Services Alteration of Terrain Permit? The amendment has been on file at the Municipal Building since December 26, 2025.

(Recommended by the Planning Board by a vote of 7-0) This amendment extends the expiration time period for excavation permits from 2 years to 5 years to better align with the requirements for Alteration of Terrain Permits often associated with excavation operations. This lessens the burden on the excavation applicants while still allowing for Planning Board oversight.

TOWN OF BOW Conservation Commission 10 Grandview Road, Bow, New Hampshire 03304 Phone (603) 223-3970 Fax (603) 225-2982 Website: www.bownh.gov Email: conservation@bownh.gov Conservation Commission Approved Minutes Monday, December 15, 2025 The regular meeting of the Bow Conservation Commission was held on Monday, December 15, 2025 at 7:00 PM in Room C of the Municipal Office building at 10 Grandview Road. Chair Sandy Crystall called the meeting to order at 7:00 PM. Members present: Sandy Crystall, Lisa Lindquist, Tom O'Donovan, Dik Dagavarian and Mary Farrell. Other attendees: Ginger Iverson, Recording Secretary. 1.

Eversource – Lots 21-5-3-A and 1-5-3 Wetland Conditional Use Permit (CUP) Application # 407-25 D-121 Transmission Line Structure Replacement Project Temporary wetland impacts (7,923 sq. ft.) for the replacement of three existing utility structures (i.e., utility poles) along the D121 Transmission Line. Ms. Crystall noted that a site walk was conducted on Friday, December 12, 2025. Lindsey Tower, CPPS of GZA Geoenvironmental, Inc. and Adam Shoukimas from Eversource Energy presented the application. Others attending were Ashley Nicoletti, Supervisor Licensing and Permitting; Donald Stokes, Community Relations Specialist;

and Brad Newell, Manager, Transmission Project Management and Construction at Eversource Energy. Ms. Tower stated that Eversource proposes to replace 3 utility poles on the D121 transmission line in Bow. Access is off of Morgan Drive along a separate Eversource ROW and it crosses a couple of wetlands. Wetlands will be temporarily impacted with timber matting and upon completion of pole replacements the timber matting will be removed, impacted wetlands will be stabilized with a mulch and seedless straw. Access will be via the existing crushed-stone gravel road. The Commission proceeded with its questions to GZA and Eversource Energy. Mr.

O’Donovan asked the applicants to explain the requirements necessary for the four wildlife species referenced in the DataCheck Results letter. Ms. Tower said Eversource coordinated with NH Fish and Game (NH F&G) for Best Management Practices. NH F&G requires immediate reporting if species are observed if work is done during a particular time of the year, NH F&G requires a qualified biologist on site. Ms. Tower said the qualified biologist would be required from spring through fall for this project. Per Ms. Tower, construction for these three structures in Bow would occur April through October. Mr. Stokes replied to Ms.

Crystall that timing for the project (Q1) is slated from mid-February to October. These requirements are incorporated in the NHDES permit. Ms. Crystall commented that the addressing DataCheck results are usually noted on the plan and Ms. Tower said they didn’t have the NH F&G Best Management Practices (BMPs) recommendations at the time they submitted the CUP to the town but the State permit was subsequently provided to the Bow Town Clerk. Conservation Commission Approved Minutes 12/15/2025 2 Ms. Crystall displayed the utility corridor using the Bow GIS. Mr. O’Donovan noted that he didn't realize that the corridor traverse town land. He asked Eversource what the utility easement allows. Mr.

Newell said they didn’t have a copy of the utility easement document this evening but generally the utility easement allows them rights and access to maintain their facilities. The Eversource representatives present introduced themselves. Mr. O’Donovan requested that Eversource provide the utility easement document for consideration by the Commission to ensure the requirements for the easement are met. Mr. O’Donovan referenced the site walk that was conducted the previous Friday and asked what the previous permits say for restoration and if Eversource met those requirements. Mr.

O’Donovan felt it was obvious where the damage to the wetlands was done previously for this project and requested that the previous permits and conditions with photographic documentation be provided to the Commission. There was discussion about what was meant by damage, and was the road visible. Mr. O’Donovan asked about how many CUPs have been obtained for this lot. Ms. Nicoletti noted that the restoration is to pre-existing conditions. Mr. O'Donovan expressed that he didn't believe that the wetlands have been restored following the emergency pole replacements (CUP 410- 24) and failed to meet the standards established by previous eﬀorts. Mr.

Newell explained Eversource’s restoration practices within wetlands and buﬀer zones. He noted that for this multiline corridor, the state likely prefers the reuse of existing, previously disturbed access areas rather than the creation of new ones during each site entry. Inspection of the utility poles are done every 1-1/2 years and age itself is not a determining factor for replacement. Ms. Nicoletti clarified that failed inspections serve as the justification needed for replacement. Mr.

O’Donovan added that the Commission has formally requested that Eversource develop a long-term strategy to end repetitive, disruptive site access as this has resulted in the cost being passed to the Commission as a natural resource impact. Mr. Stokes confirmed that a Project Engagement Specialist is coordinating with local landowners to relocate the trailers currently parked by the gate. Ms. Crystall mentioned the presence of shooting targets on this property, which is prohibited on Town-owned property. Eversource indicated that if such activities impact their facilities, they have previously been required to notify Homeland Security to intervene and stop it. Mr.

Newell said they would have Corporate Security look into it. Ms. Crystall said the Commission could notify the Bow Police Department. Eversource puts up gates and boulders to try and limit access to the area. Ms. Crystall reviewed all the documentation submitted by Eversource for application no. 407-25. Ms. Tower then summarized the site’s restoration history since 2022 and the importance of letting the area sit for a growing season or more to allow vegetative regrowth. Ms. Nicoletti recommended both pre and post site walk visits by the Commission. Mr. O’Donovan made a motion that the Conservation Commission cannot complete a full review of application 407-25 (Eversource Energy).

As required under Article 10.01(F)(2)(b), the application lacked the required utility easement and previous Conditional Use Permit (CUP) documentation. The motion was seconded by Ms. Lindquist. Vote 2:2:1 with Ms. Crystall abstaining. The motion failed to pass. Conservation Commission Approved Minutes 12/15/2025 3 Ms. Crystall commented that the commission needs to provide some input to the Planning Board consistent with CUP requirements. Mr. Dagavarian made a motion that the Conservation Commission requires the following documentation for proposed projects: 1. Utility easement information on Town land 2.

Conditional Use Permit (CUP) information along with photographic documentation from the last project in which restoration was successful according to Eversource standards. The motion was seconded by Ms. Farrell. Vote 4:0:1 with Ms. Crystall abstaining. Ms. Lindquist made a motion that the Conservation Commission reports concern regarding repetitive damage to the Wetlands Resources and Wetland Buffers, citing non-compliance with the requirements of Article 10.01(F)(2)(b) of the Zoning Ordinance of Bow. The motion was seconded by Mr. O’Donovan.

Vote 4:0:1 Eversource requested an update on when the Town's Conditional Use Permit (CUP) application will be revised to include the applicable requirements. Ms. Crystall will discuss with the Community Development Director and will follow up with Eversource directly. Mr. O’Donovan raised the issue that the Planning Board was not receiving the Commission’s reviews or specific concerns prior to the Planning Board meeting. While Ms. Crystall uploads the Conservation Commission’s motions to CloudPermit for Ms. Makinen to include in the physical Board packets, the Planning Board does not receive the information ahead of time with other Planning Board packet information. 2.

BCC Annual Report for Town report The Commission responded positively to the proposed report and suggested a few opportunities to consider to shorten certain sections. Ms. Farrell made a motion to accepted the proposed 2025 Conservation Commission Annual Report with optional amendments. The motion was seconded by Mr. Dagavarian. Vote 5:0. 3. Robertson Trail Status Chair Crystall emailed the NHDES permitting inspector for Bow concerning permitting and secured a quote from Northpoint Engineering for the Corps Functional Assessment.

The motion was seconded by Ms. Farrell. Vote: 5-0 4.
